Painting Heritage Homes in the Inner West

Federation and Victorian homes are beautiful — and unforgiving of the wrong paint. Here’s how to repaint a period home without doing it harm.

props.label: Old walls need to breathe
props.html:
BN
Bobby Nojad
Owner & painter, Painters Inner West · 20+ years

The Inner West holds some of Sydney’s finest period housing — Victorian terraces in Balmain and Glebe, Federation homes in Haberfield and Croydon, and grand Annandale mansions. Painting them well takes more than a steady hand; it takes the right products and a respect for how old buildings work.

Old walls need to breathe

Solid masonry and lath-and-plaster walls in period homes manage moisture by letting it pass through. Seal them under a modern impermeable coating and you trap that moisture, which leads to bubbling paint, salt damage and rotting timber.

The fix is breathable, conservation-appropriate coatings designed for older buildings. It’s the single most important decision on a heritage repaint — and the one most often gotten wrong.

Take lead paint seriously

Homes built before the 1970s very likely have lead-based paint under later coats. Sanding or scraping it without precautions releases lead dust that’s dangerous to your household and the neighbourhood.

Lead paint should be identified and, where disturbed, contained and removed using safe practices and proper disposal. It’s not a step to cut corners on.

Respect the era with colour

Period homes look their best in colours sympathetic to their age. Heritage and National Trust palettes exist for exactly this reason, and many Inner West streets sit in conservation areas where the streetscape matters.

Getting the scheme right — body, trim, and the fine detail of verandah posts, fretwork and iron lace — is what makes a restored period home sing.

Preparation and patience

Ornate timber, decorative render and fine detail simply take longer to prepare and finish than a flat modern wall. Rushing it shows. The reward for patience is a finish that honours the home and lasts.

Before you repaint a period home: confirm the painter uses breathable systems, follows lead-safe practice, and can work to heritage colours. A general painter treating it like a new build can do real, lasting damage.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t I use normal exterior paint on a Federation home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because solid masonry and old render need to breathe. A standard impermeable paint traps moisture inside the wall, causing bubbling, salt damage and rot. Period homes need breathable, conservation-appropriate systems.

mainEntity.name: Is lead paint really a concern in Inner West homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Most homes built before the 1970s have lead-based paint under later layers. It must be identified and, if disturbed, contained and removed safely — it’s a genuine health hazard when sanded or scraped carelessly.
